If a write or restart has an uncertain result, the guide stops. Restarting the guide **does not repeat that action**. Keep the onn in its current state and preserve the saved receipts for inspection. If a completed result was saved before the terminal closed, the guide can continue after that completed step. Ordinary connection failures and read-only checks can be checked again. Keep the repository's `work/` folder. It contains device identities, acceptance, progress, attempt records and backups. A completed guide reports its last saved successful result when reopened; that is not a fresh live device check. ### Remove temporary leftovers and start again If an upload or temporary-system installation was interrupted, the guide offers **Remove temporary system and start again**. Each restart uses new temporary-system attempt records; old receipts cannot authorize the new attempt. A fresh clone can remove device-side leftovers with this option, but cannot recover records that were deleted. Keep your original work folder. This option refuses an attempted permanent-root write, an existing permanent-root installation, a running/enabled guest, or an unresolved reboot on the same boot. It does not bypass firmware or stock-image checks. If cleanup loses its connection, rerun the guide to inspect the current state and explicitly confirm recovery again. See [recovery and failure handling](docs/RECOVERY.md) before changing a device whose firmware write or reboot is uncertain. ### The two temporary boots The **first DSU boot is a test** to check that temporary Android starts and that the onn can return to original Android. Observe the setup screen, skip setup, sign-in and debugging settings, then follow the prompt to power-cycle once back into original Android. **Root is not installed during this test.** The guide checks the original system after it returns, then prepares and starts a second DSU boot for root installation. ADB inside the test system is not required. The **second DSU boot is for root installation**: pair the remote if needed, connect Ethernet or Wi-Fi, and **stay in this system with the power on**. This image already starts network ADB on **port 5555** with the computer's public key included. Continue in the guide once the network is connected so it can try that prepared connection before you open debugging settings or sign in to Google. Google account setup is not a step in this guide. If it cannot connect, use the reconnection screen's debugging/pairing instructions as troubleshooting. ## More than one onn, or a changed IP Use the same guide for multiple supported **2026** units, **one at a time**. Choose the intended unit from the saved-device list, or choose **Add another onn**. Each has its own serial, progress, prepared images, backups and attempt records. Stock downloads can be reused. The older 2024 onn needs its separate installer. **Enter the IP address once when adding each new onn.** The first connection does not automatically discover new units. Once saved, the guide can look for that same onn automatically after an address change. Room names are yours to choose; leaving the name blank uses the hardware serial. Before a device action, the guide checks the saved serial, firmware, bootloader and slot. After an IP change it looks for that same unit. Another onn taking the old address is rejected, even if its firmware is identical. If discovery cannot confirm one device, the guide asks you to check Wi-Fi/debugging or enter its new address; it does not select a different onn automatically. When the saved address is unavailable, discovery also checks ADB's mDNS advertisements for a changed wireless connection port and tries the prepared image's port 5555 at the saved IP. Paired devices are recognized when ADB lists their connection service name instead of an IP address. Pairing ports are excluded, and a discovered address must pass the same device checks. If multicast discovery is unavailable (including some WSL2 networks), enter the **IP:connection-port** shown on the TV. If pairing is needed, run `adb pair IP:PAIRING_PORT` in another terminal and enter the code shown on the TV, then use the separate connection port in the guide. See [Android's wireless ADB instructions](https://developer.android.com/tools/adb#connect-to-a-device-over-wi-fi). ## Preview and advanced use For a text overview without contacting any device: ```sh python3 onn2026.py guide --preview ``` The [advanced command reference](docs/MANUAL.md) retains the individual commands for inspection and reviewed manual work. Use `python3 onn2026.py --help` for options such as a custom ADB path. Do not mix manual mutations into an active guide. ## If the temporary-system build stops `build-offline-dsu` prepares the temporary Android images on your computer. Build time depends on CPU and storage speed. This step now shows its current stage and compression progress and has a **15-minute overall limit**. A tool failure stops it immediately. Reaching the limit or pressing Ctrl-C stops the build and its tools and preserves the logs. After a failed or cancelled build, run the same guide command from the same checkout and keep the existing `work/` folder. The guide retries the local build in a fresh session and reuses the completed unlock and on-device patch records. It will only stage a temporary system after the new build passes validation. For a tool failure, the error gives its exit code and the combined `NNN-build-offline-dsu.log` path. The named tool log under that session's `dsu-build/` directory contains the tool's detailed output. Existing timeout receipts from older versions remain available for diagnosis. If `fsck.erofs` reports that `--extract` does not allow an argument, its version cannot extract files into a directory. Upgrade the computer's EROFS tools using [these instructions](docs/HOST_TOOLS.md), then resume the guide. ## Collect a slot-A diagnostic report For a compatibility question such as [issue #2](https://github.com/openensemble/onn-4k-pro-2026-unlock-root/issues/2), run the separate read-only collector. It accepts **slot A or B**, including a locked 2026 `jarvis2`. The report distinguishes slots accepted by the installer from slots with hardware-verified unlock/root results. Only Python 3.10+ and Android platform-tools (`adb`) are needed; no root, NDK or firmware download is required. Enable debugging on the onn, then replace `ONN_IP` with its IP address: ```sh python3 tools/slot_report.py --target ONN_IP ``` The default ADB port is 5555; use `--target ONN_IP:PORT` if needed. Accept the debugging prompt on that onn and rerun if the collector reports unauthorized. Use `--adb /path/to/adb` for a custom executable. It connects only to the address you specify and checks the same physical unit, firmware, slot and boot throughout collection. Optional `--expect-serial SERIAL` also checks the initial physical identity. Neither the address nor serial appears in the shareable report. The collector reads firmware and AVB properties, both slots' partition mappings, accessible partition sizes, available boot-control/update status, and init_boot hashes when ordinary shell access and the expected partition length permit it. Permission denials and missing tools are recorded as unavailable information. An unreadable partition is not evidence that the slot is damaged or unsupported. Results are saved in a new ignored `work/slot-reports/` directory: - **`slot-report.txt` or `slot-report.json`:** review and attach one to the issue. These contain selected diagnostic facts, with address, serial and boot ID omitted. - **`private.json`:** raw command receipts containing device identifiers; keep this file local. Do not attach the entire output directory. This script does not request root, install an app, write settings or firmware, reboot, switch slots, or run the unlock installer. A completed report means the collection finished; it does **not** establish that slot A is safe to unlock/root or that the inactive slot contains a usable installation. Leave the firmware profile and active slot unchanged when collecting a report. ## What was tested The underlying unlock, DSU return, DSU root console, single init_boot flash, readback, Magisk setup and subsequent root were measured on one supported unit. The packaged builder completed a clean build and metadata/content round trip; its helper’s loaded ELF sections match the tested helper for the same binding. The packaged permanent-root verifier was also run on that unit. The host tests cover identity/slot/boot mismatches, prior attempts, enable/reboot failures, interrupted writes, changed IP addresses, other onns at an old address, unauthorized devices, ambiguous identities and separate household profiles. The guide tests also cover required risk acceptance, saving progress, resuming confirmed results, and refusing to repeat uncertain operations. The new guide, automatic restarts and reconnect behavior have been tested with simulated device responses. See the [validation details and rebuild commands](docs/BUILD.md). ## What was not tested - Recovery after a power loss or an unbootable modified `init_boot` image. Passing the tests does not guarantee bug-free behavior or recovery from a failed installation. See the [recovery limitations](docs/RECOVERY.md). ## Licenses See [third-party license information](THIRD_PARTY.md).

from contextlib import redirect_stdout

MKFS, FSCK = shutil.which("mkfs.erofs"), shutil.which("fsck.erofs")


class ErofsToolTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.folder = Path(self.tmp.name)

    def tool(self, name, source):
        path = self.folder / name
        path.write_text("#!" + sys.executable + "\n" + source)
        path.chmod(0o755)
        return str(path)

    @unittest.skipUnless(MKFS and FSCK, "Install erofs-utils for the actual tool round trip")
    def test_actual_tools_build_and_extract_compressed_files_and_symlinks(self):
        temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory
        with patch.object(erofs_tools.tempfile, "TemporaryDirectory",
                          side_effect=lambda **kwargs: temporary(dir=self.folder, **kwargs)):
            erofs_tools.check_erofs_tools(MKFS, FSCK)
        self.assertEqual(list(self.folder.iterdir()), [])

    @unittest.skipUnless(MKFS, "Install erofs-utils for the extraction fixtures")
    def test_legacy_extract_option_error_includes_selected_tool_and_upgrade(self):
        old = self.tool("old-fsck", "import sys\n"
                        "print('option --extract does not allow an argument', file=sys.stderr)\nsys.exit(1)\n")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(o.Stop, "--extract does not allow an argument") as stopped:
            erofs_tools.check_erofs_tools(MKFS, old)
        self.assertIn(old, str(stopped.exception))
        self.assertIn("docs/HOST_TOOLS.md", str(stopped.exception))

    @unittest.skipUnless(MKFS, "Install erofs-utils for the extraction fixtures")
    def test_successful_integrity_check_without_extracted_files_is_rejected(self):
        no_extract = self.tool("check-only-fsck", "print('image integrity checked')\n")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(o.Stop, "did not extract the expected files"):
            erofs_tools.check_erofs_tools(MKFS, no_extract)

    def test_missing_tar_support_stops_before_extraction(self):
        old = self.tool("old-mkfs", "import sys\nprint('unrecognized option --tar=f', file=sys.stderr)\nsys.exit(1)\n")
        marker = self.folder / "fsck-ran"
        unused = self.tool("unused-fsck", f"from pathlib import Path\nPath({str(marker)!r}).touch()\n")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(o.Stop, "unrecognized option --tar=f"):
            erofs_tools.check_erofs_tools(old, unused)
        self.assertFalse(marker.exists())

    def test_guide_rejects_incompatible_tools_during_host_setup(self):
        args = SimpleNamespace(mkfs_erofs="mkfs.erofs", fsck_erofs="fsck.erofs", secilc="secilc")
        with patch.object(guide.platform, "system", return_value="Linux"), \
             patch.object(guide.platform, "machine", return_value="x86_64"), \
             patch.object(guide.shutil, "which", return_value="/fixture/tool"), \
             patch.object(guide, "check_erofs_tools", side_effect=o.Stop("incompatible EROFS tools")):
            # No NDK selection or other setup may be attempted after this fails.
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(o.Stop, "incompatible EROFS tools"):
                guide.host_setup(args, None)

    def test_direct_or_resumed_builder_checks_tools_before_reading_inputs(self):
        args = SimpleNamespace(mkfs_erofs="mkfs.erofs", fsck_erofs="fsck.erofs", serial="JUSATOOLTEST", slot="_b")
        with patch.object(build_dsu, "check_erofs_tools", side_effect=o.Stop("incompatible EROFS tools")), \
             redirect_stdout(StringIO()):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(o.Stop, "incompatible EROFS tools"):
                build_dsu.build(args)

    def test_stuck_probe_has_a_bounded_wait_and_upgrade_diagnostic(self):
        def timeout(argv, **kwargs):
            self.assertEqual(kwargs["timeout"], 30)
            raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(argv, kwargs["timeout"])
        with patch.object(erofs_tools.subprocess, "run", side_effect=timeout):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(o.Stop, "docs/HOST_TOOLS.md"):
                erofs_tools.run_probe(["fixture-tool"], "check a tiny image")

"""Compile the actual unlock entry point with a host property stub that stops before device I/O."""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PROFILE = json.loads((ROOT / "profile.json").read_text())
ROW = PROFILE["variants"]["jarvis2-row-15016191"]


class NativeIdentity(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        if not shutil.which("cc"):
            raise unittest.SkipTest("A host C compiler is needed for native identity guards")
        temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        cls.addClassCleanup(temporary.cleanup)
        root = Path(temporary.name)
        (root / "sys").mkdir()
        (root / "sys/system_properties.h").write_text(
            "#define PROP_VALUE_MAX 92\nint __system_property_get(const char *, char *);\n")
        stub = root / "android-stub.c"
        stub.write_text(
            "#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <sys/types.h>\n"
            "uid_t getuid(void) { const char *v = getenv(\"ONN26_FIXTURE_UID\"); return v ? atoi(v) : 2000; }\n"
            "uid_t geteuid(void) { return getuid(); }\n"
            # No property ever matches: execution stops before boot-ID, marker or TEE access.
            "int __system_property_get(const char *key, char *out) { (void)key; out[0] = 0; return 0; }\n")
        cls.binary = root / "unlock-entry-fixture"
        subprocess.run(["cc", "-std=c11", "-D_GNU_SOURCE", "-O2", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Werror",
                        "-I", str(root), str(ROOT / "native/unlock_once.c"), str(stub),
                        "-o", str(cls.binary)], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)

    def entry(self, serial, profile, slot="_a", uid="2000", marker="/data/local/tmp/oe26-avb-fixture/consumed"):
        result = subprocess.run([str(self.binary), "--unlock-once", serial, profile["fingerprint"],
                                 profile["bootloader"], slot, "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555", marker],
                                env={**os.environ, "ONN26_FIXTURE_UID": uid}, capture_output=True,
                                text=True, timeout=5)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, "", "No trusted-state request may reach a real device")
        return result

    def test_us_and_row_reach_exact_property_checks_on_both_slots(self):
        for profile in (PROFILE, ROW):
            for slot in ("_a", "_b"):
                with self.subTest(profile=profile["id"], slot=slot):
                    result = self.entry(profile["serial_prefixes"][0] + "NATIVETEST001", profile, slot)
                    self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 22)
                    self.assertIn("Identity mismatch: ro.product.device", result.stderr)

    def test_missing_malformed_and_cross_region_serials_fail_before_properties(self):
        cases = [("JCA", ROW), ("JUSA", PROFILE), ("", ROW), ("JCATEST_001", ROW),
                 ("JCATEST;id", ROW), ("JCATEST001", PROFILE), ("JUSATEST001", ROW),
                 ("SNATEST001", ROW), ("JCATest\n", ROW)]
        for serial, profile in cases:
            with self.subTest(serial=serial, profile=profile["id"]):
                self.assertEqual(self.entry(serial, profile).returncode, 21)

    def test_caller_and_marker_guards_still_apply_to_both_regions(self):
        for profile in (PROFILE, ROW):
            serial = profile["serial_prefixes"][0] + "NATIVETEST001"
            for uid in ("0", "1000"):
                with self.subTest(profile=profile["id"], uid=uid):
                    self.assertEqual(self.entry(serial, profile, uid=uid).returncode, 21)
            for marker in ("/tmp/fixture", "/data/local/tmp/oe26-avb-fixture/../consumed"):
                with self.subTest(profile=profile["id"], marker=marker):
                    self.assertEqual(self.entry(serial, profile, marker=marker).returncode, 21)

"""Accept Android's unpadded hexadecimal IDs without weakening identity checks."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
import tempfile
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch

import onn2026 as o
import root_workflow as flow

BOOT = "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555"
BINDING = {"ro.serialno": "JUSAIDENTITYTEST", "ro.product.device": o.PROFILE["device"],
           "ro.build.fingerprint": o.PROFILE["fingerprint"], "ro.bootloader": o.PROFILE["bootloader"],
           "ro.boot.slot_suffix": "_b"}


class BeforeDeviceWrite(Exception):
    pass


class Device:
    def __init__(self, directory, android_id):
        self.s = o.Session(directory, "android-id-fixture")
        self.binding = dict(BINDING)
        self.android_id = android_id
        self.calls = []

    def identify(self, **kwargs):
        assert kwargs == {"unlocked": True}
        return dict(self.binding)

    def boot_id(self):
        return BOOT

    def text(self, label, *args, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append((label, args))
        assert args == ("settings", "get", "secure", "android_id")
        return self.android_id

    def shell(self, label, *args, **kwargs):
        # These boundaries precede any actual staging. This fake never sends
        # commands or transfers files to a device.
        if label == "mkdir-patch":
            raise BeforeDeviceWrite()
        if label == "staging-name-unused":
            return {"returncode": 0, "timed_out": False, "stdout": ""}
        raise AssertionError("Unexpected device command: " + label)

    def call(self, label, *args, **kwargs):
        if label == "push-dsu":
            raise BeforeDeviceWrite()
        raise AssertionError("Unexpected ADB action: " + label)


class AndroidIdentityTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        # Any escape from a fake device is an error, including the trusted reader.
        guard = patch.object(o.subprocess, "run", side_effect=AssertionError("Live I/O forbidden"))
        guard.start()
        self.addCleanup(guard.stop)

    def prepare(self, value):

import os

import unittest


class TerminalButtons(unittest.TestCase):
    def choose(self, keys, expected):
        master, slave = pty.openpty()
        original = termios.tcgetattr(slave)
        process = None
        try:
            process = subprocess.Popen(
                [sys.executable, "-B", "-c", "from console_ui import accept_decline; print('RESULT=' + str(accept_decline()), flush=True)"],
                stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, cwd=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1], close_fds=True)
            output = b""
            deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
            sent = False
            while b"RESULT=" not in output and time.monotonic() < deadline:
                if select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)[0]:
                    output += os.read(master, 4096)
                if not sent and b"Decline" in output:
                    os.write(master, keys)
                    sent = True
            process.wait(timeout=3)
            self.assertEqual(process.returncode, 0, output)
            self.assertIn(("RESULT=" + str(expected)).encode(), output)
            self.assertEqual(termios.tcgetattr(slave), original, "Terminal settings were not restored")
        finally:
            if process is not None and process.poll() is None:
                process.kill()
                process.wait()
            os.close(master)
            os.close(slave)

def image_bytes(marker):
    data = bytearray(b"\0" * 8388608)
    data[:8] = b"ANDROID!"
    struct.pack_into("<II", data, 8, 0, 1024)
    struct.pack_into("<I", data, 40, 4)
    data[4096:4100] = marker
    return bytes(data)


class Android(o.Device):
    def __init__(self, work, slot):
        self.s = o.Session(work, "slot-fixture")
        self.target, self.adb, self.connection_path = "192.0.2.80:5555", "/offline-adb", None
        self.props = {"ro.serialno": "JUSASLOTTEST", "ro.product.device": o.PROFILE["device"],
                      "ro.build.fingerprint": o.PROFILE["fingerprint"], "ro.bootloader": o.PROFILE["bootloader"],
                      "ro.product.cpu.abilist": o.PROFILE["abi"], "ro.boot.slot_suffix": slot,
                      "sys.boot_completed": "1", **o.UNLOCKED}
        self.binding = None
        self.identify()
        name, block = TARGETS[slot]
        self.partition, self.block = "/dev/block/by-name/" + name, "/dev/block/" + block
        self.other = "/dev/block/by-name/init_boot" + ("_b" if slot == "_a" else "_a")
        self.boot, self.dsu = BOOT, "running\ninstalled\ndisabled"
        self.image, self.patch_image = image_bytes(b"STOK"), image_bytes(b"ROOT")
        self.helper_hash, self.calls, self.flashes, self.reboots = "c" * 64, [], 0, 0
        self.hash_output_path = self.partition

    def text(self, label, *args, **kwargs):
        if args == ("getprop",):
            return "\n".join(f"[{k}]: [{v}]" for k, v in self.props.items())
        if args == ("cat", "/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id"):
            return self.boot
        if args == ("gsi_tool", "status"):
            return self.dsu
        if args == ("settings", "get", "secure", "android_id"):
            return ANDROID_ID
        if args == ("sha256sum", "/system/bin/onn26-su"):
            return self.helper_hash + "  /system/bin/onn26-su"
        raise AssertionError((label, args))

    def check_partition_command(self, command):
        assert self.other not in command, command
        assert self.partition in command and self.block in command, command
        assert 'test "$(getprop ro.boot.slot_suffix)" = ' + self.binding["ro.boot.slot_suffix"] in command
        assert '/sys/class/block/' + self.block.rsplit('/', 1)[1] + '/size' in command

    def shell(self, label, *args, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append((label, args))
        stdout = ""
        if label in ("root-and-stock-proof", "before-root-reboot-readback", "verify-permanent-root"):
            self.check_partition_command(args[2])
            line = hashlib.sha256(self.image).hexdigest() + "  " + self.hash_output_path + "\n"
            stdout = line
            if label == "root-and-stock-proof":
                stdout = "uid=0(root) gid=0(root) context=u:r:onn26_root:s0\n" + line
            if label == "verify-permanent-root":
                stdout = ("uid=0(root) gid=0(root) context=u:r:magisk:s0\n"
                          "30.7:MAGISK:R\n30700\nEnforcing\n" + line + "MAGISK_ENVIRONMENT_COMPLETE\n")
        elif label == "native-preflight-no-write":
            stdout = "PREFLIGHT_VERIFIED\n"
        elif label == "flash-once":
            assert flow.read(flow.journal(self, "root-install-attempt.json"))["binding"] == self.binding
            self.flashes += 1
            self.image = self.patch_image
            stdout = "FLASH_READBACK_VERIFIED\n" + hashlib.sha256(self.image).hexdigest() + "\n"
        elif label == "unlock-once":
            assert args[5] == self.binding["ro.boot.slot_suffix"], args
            assert flow.journal(self, "unlock-attempt.json").exists()
            stdout = json.dumps({"stage": "finished", "outcome": 0, "write_invocations": 1})
        elif label not in ("mkdir-root-staging", "readable-root-input", "remove-used-flasher",
                           "flush-before-normal-reboot", "mkdir-writer", "chmod-writer", "remove-writer"):
            raise AssertionError((label, args))
        return {"returncode": 0, "timed_out": False, "stdout": stdout, "stderr": ""}

    def push_checked(self, source, remote):
        self.calls.append(("push", (str(source), remote)))

    def call(self, label, *args, **kwargs):
        assert args == ("reboot",)
        self.reboots += 1
        return {"returncode": 0, "timed_out": False, "stdout": "", "stderr": ""}

    def backup_transport(self, argv, **kwargs):
        assert argv[:4] == [self.adb, "-s", self.target, "exec-out"]
        helper, flag, command = shlex.split(argv[4])

class FakeADB:
    def __init__(self, slot="_a", readable=False):
        self.values = {key: "" for key in sr.PROPERTIES}
        self.values.update({
            "ro.serialno": SERIAL, "boot_id": BOOT,
            "ro.product.device": "jarvis2", "ro.product.model": "onn 4K Pro Streaming Device",

            "ro.boot.flash.locked": "1", "ro.boot.vbmeta.device_state": "locked",
            "ro.boot.verifiedbootstate": "green", "sys.boot_completed": "1",
        })
        self.readable = readable
        self.calls = []
        self.queries = []
        self.identity_count = 0
        self.overrides = {}
        self.final_changes = {}
        self.guard_fails = False
        self.connect_unauthorized = False

    def __call__(self, argv, **kwargs):
        assert kwargs["shell"] is False
        assert kwargs["timeout"] == 10
        self.calls.append(argv)
        if argv == ["fake-adb", "connect", TARGET]:
            output = "failed to authenticate to " + TARGET if self.connect_unauthorized else "connected to " + TARGET
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, output, "")
        assert argv[:4] == ["fake-adb", "-s", TARGET, "shell"], "Unselected target or non-shell ADB action"
        assert len(argv) == 5
        script = argv[4]
        if script == sr.IDENTITY_COMMAND:
            self.identity_count += 1
            values = dict(self.values)
            if self.identity_count > 1:
                values.update(self.final_changes)
            output = "\n".join(key + "=" + value for key, value in values.items()) + "\n"
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, output, "")
        guard, command = script.rsplit("\n", 1)
        assert "|| exit 90" in guard and self.values["ro.serialno"] in guard and BOOT in guard
        query = tuple(shlex.split(command))
        self.queries.append(query)
        if self.guard_fails:
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 90, "", "")
        if query in self.overrides:
            value = self.overrides[query]
            if isinstance(value, BaseException):
                raise value
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, *value)
        if query == ("id", "-u"):
            response = (0, "2000\n", "")
        elif query == ("getenforce",):
            response = (0, "Enforcing\n", "")
        elif query == ("cat", "/proc/partitions"):
            response = (0, "179 22 8192 mmcblk0p22\n179 23 8192 mmcblk0p23\n", "") if self.readable else (
                1, "", "Permission denied " + SERIAL + " " + BOOT + " " + TARGET)
        elif query[0] == "readlink":
            assert query[:2] == ("readlink", "-f")
            name = query[2].removeprefix("/dev/block/by-name/")
            assert name in NODES and len(query) == 3
            response = (0, "/dev/block/mmcblk0p" + str(NODES[name]) + "\n", "")
        elif query[0] == "cat":
            assert len(query) == 2 and query[1] in {
                f"/sys/class/block/mmcblk0p{node}/size" for node in NODES.values()}
            response = (0, "16384\n", "") if self.readable else (1, "", "Permission denied")
        elif query[0] == "sha256sum":
            assert self.readable and query[1] in ("/dev/block/by-name/init_boot_a", "/dev/block/by-name/init_boot_b")
            assert len(query) == 2
            response = (0, PROFILE["init_boot_sha256"] + "  " + query[1] + "\n", "")
        elif query[0] == "bootctl":
            allowed = {("bootctl", command) for command in (
                "get-number-slots", "get-current-slot", "get-active-boot-slot", "get-snapshot-merge-status")}
            allowed |= {("bootctl", command, slot) for command in
                        ("is-slot-bootable", "is-slot-marked-successful") for slot in ("0", "1")}
            assert query in allowed, "Mutating or unknown bootctl command"
            if self.readable:
                output = {"get-number-slots": "2\n", "get-current-slot": "0\n",
                          "get-active-boot-slot": "0\n", "get-snapshot-merge-status": "none\n"}.get(query[1], "")
                response = (0, output, "")
            else:
                response = (127, "", "bootctl: not found " + TARGET + " " + SERIAL)
        elif query == ("update_engine_client", "--status"):
            response = (0, "CURRENT_OP=UPDATE_STATUS_IDLE\nUPDATE_URL=https://private.example/" + SERIAL, "")
        elif query == ("gsi_tool", "status"):
            response = (0, "normal\n", "")
        else:
            raise AssertionError("Unexpected or mutating device query: " + repr(query))
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, *response)

def image(path, marker):
    header = bytearray(4096)
    header[:8] = b"ANDROID!"
    struct.pack_into("<II", header, 8, 0, 64)
    struct.pack_into("<I", header, 40, 4)
    with path.open("wb") as output:
        output.write(header)
        output.write(marker)
        output.truncate(o.PROFILE["init_boot_size"])
    return path


class Device(RegionalDevice):
    def __init__(self, work, patched, slot="_a"):
        self.boot, self.android_id, self.dsu = BOOT, "123456789abcdef", "normal"
        self.patched, self.proof_override, self.boot_after_proof = patched, None, None
        super().__init__(work, slot)

    def text(self, label, *args, **kwargs):
        if args == ("cat", "/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id"):
            return self.boot
        if args == ("settings", "get", "secure", "android_id"):
            return self.android_id
        if args == ("gsi_tool", "status"):
            return self.dsu
        if label == "read-patch-config":
            return CONFIG
        return super().text(label, *args, **kwargs)

    def call(self, label, *args, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append((label, *args))
        if label == "pull-patched-image":
            assert args[0] == "pull" and args[1].endswith("/new-boot.img")
            shutil.copyfile(self.patched, args[2])
            return {"returncode": 0, "timed_out": False, "stdout": "", "stderr": ""}
        raise AssertionError("Unexpected ADB command: " + label)

    def shell(self, label, *args, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append((label, *args))
        result = {"returncode": 0, "timed_out": False, "stdout": "", "stderr": ""}
        if label == "cpio-test":
            return {**result, "returncode": 1}
        if label == "manager-presence":
            return {**result, "stdout": "package:/fixture/Magisk.apk"}
        if label == "verify-permanent-root":
            if self.boot_after_proof:
                self.boot = self.boot_after_proof
            return self.proof_override or {**result, "stdout":
                "uid=0(root) gid=0(root) context=u:r:magisk:s0\n30.7:MAGISK:R\n30700\nEnforcing\n"
                + o.digest(self.patched) + "  " + o.root_partition(self.binding)
                + "\nMAGISK_ENVIRONMENT_COMPLETE\n"}
        assert label in {"mkdir-patch", "chmod-busybox", "patch-local-image-only", "mkdir-verify",
                         "unpack-patch-check", "extract-config", "read-own-config-mode", "remove-own-staging"}, label
        return result

class FakeBackend:
    def __init__(self, work, locked=True, binding=None):
        self.work, self.locked = Path(work), locked
        self.binding = dict(binding or BINDING)
        self.calls, self.prepared = [], []
        self.failures, self.answers = {}, {}
        self.connection_failure = None
        self.interrupt = None

    def prepare(self, phase):
        self.prepared.append(phase)
        if phase == self.connection_failure:
            raise o.Stop("simulated disconnected device before action")
        return SimpleNamespace(s=o.Session(self.work, "fake-guide-" + phase), device=None)

    def invoke(self, phase, context, values):
        self.calls.append((phase, values))
        if phase in self.failures:
            raise self.failures[phase]
        if phase == self.interrupt:
            signal.getsignal(signal.SIGINT)(signal.SIGINT, None)
        if phase in self.answers:
            answer = self.answers[phase]
            return answer.pop(0) if isinstance(answer, list) else answer
        canned = {
            "host": {"ndk": "/example/ndk", "adb_public_key": "/example/adbkey.pub",
                     "mkfs_erofs": "mkfs.erofs", "fsck_erofs": "fsck.erofs", "secilc": "secilc"},
            "baseline": {"binding": self.binding, "boot_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
                         "secure_lock_state": int(self.locked), "unlocked_on_current_boot": not self.locked,
                         "write_invocations": 0},
            "unlock": {"binding": self.binding, "boot_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
                       "write_invocations": 1, "secure_lock_state": 0},
            "unlock_reboot": {"reboot_requests": 1, "already_rebooted": False, "transport": {"timed_out": True}},
            "install_reboot": {"reboot_requests": 1, "already_rebooted": False, "transport": {"timed_out": True}},
            "unlocked_check": {"secure_lock_state": 0, "unlocked_on_current_boot": True},
            "fetch": {"stock_init_boot": "/example/stock.img", "magisk_apk": "/example/Magisk.apk"},
            "patch": {"patch_result": "/example/patch.json"}, "build": {"build": "/example/build.json"},
            "stock_stage": {"stage": "/example/stock-stage.json"},
            "root_stage": {"stage": "/example/root-stage.json"},
            "stock_wait": {"installed_disabled_verified": True}, "root_wait": {"installed_disabled_verified": True},
            "stock_boot": {"reboot_requests": 1, "transport": {"timed_out": True}},
            "root_boot": {"reboot_requests": 1, "transport": {"timed_out": True}},
            "stock_return": {"rehearsal": "/example/return.json"}, "root_ready": {"temporary_system_ready": True},
            "install": {"verified_flash": True, "install_result": "/example/install.json", "boot_id": "root-guest"},
            "normal_check": {"boot_id": "original-before-magisk"}, "verify": {"root_verified": True},
            "cleanup": {"cleanup_completed": True}, "updates": {"automatic_system_updates_disabled": True},
            "updates_check": {"automatic_system_updates_disabled": True},
        }
        if phase not in canned:
            raise AssertionError("Unexpected guide operation: " + phase)
        return canned[phase]

    def count(self, phase):
        return sum(name == phase for name, _ in self.calls)

           "ro.build.fingerprint": o.PROFILE["fingerprint"], "ro.bootloader": o.PROFILE["bootloader"],
           "ro.boot.slot_suffix": "_b"}
ARCHIVE = "/storage/emulated/0/Download/onn26-stock-123456789abc.raw.gz"


class Android:
    def __init__(self, work):
        self.work = work
        self.binding = dict(BINDING)
        self.props = {**self.binding, **o.UNLOCKED, "ro.product.cpu.abilist": o.PROFILE["abi"],
                      "sys.boot_completed": "1"}
        self.s = o.Session(work, "restart-fixture")
        self.boot_number = 1
        self.android_id = "123456789abcdef"
        self.state = "installed\ndisabled"
        self.files = {ARCHIVE: b"part of an interrupted upload"}
        self.symlinks = set()
        self.root = False
        self.calls, self.writes = [], []
        self.hook = lambda label: None
        self.log = ""

    def prepare(self, phase):
        self.s = o.Session(self.work, "fixture-" + phase)
        return SimpleNamespace(s=self.s, device=self)

    def identify(self, unlocked=False):
        binding = o.validate_identity(self.props, unlocked)
        o.require(binding == self.binding, "Physical device or firmware differs from the saved binding")
        return self.props

    def boot_id(self):
        return f"11111111-2222-3333-4444-{self.boot_number:012d}"

    def text(self, label, *args, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append((label, args))
        self.hook(label)
        if args == ("gsi_tool", "status"):
            return self.state
        if args == ("settings", "get", "secure", "android_id"):
            return self.android_id
        if label == "restart-downloads":
            return "\n".join(p for p in self.files if p.startswith("/storage/emulated/0/Download/onn26-"))
        if args[:3] == ("stat", "-c", "%s"):
            return str(len(self.files[args[3]]))
        if args[0] == "sha256sum":
            return hashlib.sha256(self.files[args[1]]).hexdigest() + "  " + args[1]
        if args[0] == "logcat":
            return self.log
        raise AssertionError((label, args))

    def shell(self, label, *args, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append((label, args))
        self.hook(label)
        result = {"returncode": 0, "timed_out": False, "stdout": ""}
        if label == "restart-existing-root":
            result["returncode"] = 0 if self.root else 1
        elif label == "restart-download-type":
            result["returncode"] = int(any(p in args[-1] for p in self.symlinks))
        elif label == "staging-name-unused":
            result["returncode"] = int(args[-1] in self.files)
        elif label in ("stop-dsu-installer", "remove-abandoned-dsu", "remove-abandoned-upload"):
            assert recovery.pending(recovery.directory(self)), "Missing durable recovery intent"
            self.writes.append(label)
            if label == "remove-abandoned-dsu":
                assert args == ("gsi_tool", "wipe")
                self.state = "normal"
            if label == "remove-abandoned-upload":
                name = shlex.split(args[-1])[-1]
                assert recovery.DOWNLOAD.fullmatch(name)
                assert hashlib.sha256(self.files[name]).hexdigest() in args[-1], "Changed upload must not be deleted"
                del self.files[name]
        elif label == "stage-disabled-dsu":
            self.writes.append(label)
            self.state = "installed\ndisabled"
            name = args[args.index("-d") + 1].rsplit("/", 1)[1]
            self.log = name + "\nstatus: READY, cause: INSTALL_COMPLETED"
        elif label == "enable-single-use-dsu":
            self.writes.append(label)
            self.state = "installed\nenabled"
        elif label != "flush-single-use-state":
            raise AssertionError((label, args))
        return result

    def call(self, label, *args, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append((label, args))
        self.hook(label)
        self.writes.append(label)
        if label == "push-dsu":
            self.files[args[2]] = Path(args[1]).read_bytes()
        elif label == "single-dsu-reboot":
            self.boot_number += 1
            self.state = "running\ninstalled\ndisabled"
        else:
            raise AssertionError((label, args))
        return {"returncode": 0, "timed_out": False, "stdout": ""}

class FakeSession(o.Session):
    def __init__(self, work, connected=None, available=None, properties=None, mdns="", mdns_failed=False, aliases=None):
        super().__init__(work, "offline-reconnect-test")
        self.connected = dict(connected or {})
        self.available = dict(available or {})
        self.properties = dict(properties or {})
        self.calls = []
        self.reads = {}
        self.on_read = lambda target, count: None
        self.mdns, self.mdns_failed = mdns, mdns_failed
        self.aliases = dict(aliases or {})

    def run(self, label, argv, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append(list(argv))
        if argv[:2] == ["fake-adb", "connect"] and len(argv) == 3:
            if argv[2] in self.available:
                self.connected[self.aliases.get(argv[2], argv[2])] = self.available[argv[2]]
            output = ""
        elif argv == ["fake-adb", "devices", "-l"]:
            output = "List of devices attached\n" + "\n".join(
                f"{target}\t{state}" for target, state in self.connected.items())
        elif argv == ["fake-adb", "mdns", "services"]:
            return {"returncode": 1 if self.mdns_failed else 0, "timed_out": self.mdns_failed,
                    "stdout": self.mdns, "stderr": ""}
        elif len(argv) == 5 and argv[:2] == ["fake-adb", "-s"] and argv[3:] == ["shell", "getprop"]:
            target = argv[2]
            if self.connected.get(target) != "device":
                raise AssertionError("Properties read from unauthorized/offline device")
            self.reads[target] = self.reads.get(target, 0) + 1
            self.on_read(target, self.reads[target])
            values = self.properties[target]
            if isinstance(values, list):
                values = values[min(self.reads[target] - 1, len(values) - 1)]
            output = "\n".join(f"[{key}]: [{value}]" for key, value in values.items())
        else:
            raise AssertionError("Unexpected or mutating command: " + repr(argv))
        return {"returncode": 0, "timed_out": False, "stdout": output, "stderr": ""}

    def __init__(self, work, slot="_a"):
        self.s = o.Session(work, "row-fixture")

        self.props, self.binding, self.calls = props(slot), None, []

                       "stdout": json.dumps({"stage": "finished", "outcome": 0, "write_invocations": 1})}

    def text(self, label, *args, **kwargs):
        if args == ("getprop",):
            return "\n".join(f"[{key}]: [{value}]" for key, value in self.props.items())
        if args == ("cat", "/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id"):
            return BOOT
        raise AssertionError((label, args))

    def push_checked(self, source, remote):
        self.calls.append(("push", str(source), remote))

    def shell(self, label, *args, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append((label, *args))
        if label == "unlock-once":
            attempts = list(self.s.work.glob("devices/*/unlock-attempt.json"))
            assert len(attempts) == 1, "Writer invoked without durable attempt"
            assert json.loads(attempts[0].read_text())["binding"] == self.binding
            return self.result
        if label in ("mkdir-writer", "chmod-writer", "remove-writer"):
            return {"returncode": 0, "timed_out": False, "stdout": ""}
        raise AssertionError("Unexpected mutation: " + label)

# Compatible EROFS host tools

The DSU build uses `mkfs.erofs --tar=f` with LZ4HC compression and
`fsck.erofs --extract=DIR --no-preserve`. **erofs-utils 1.7.1 is tested.** The guide
checks these capabilities by building and extracting a tiny image before
unlocking. The standalone builder repeats the check, including on resumed runs.

Older `fsck.erofs` versions use `--extract` only to check encoded file data.
They reject a destination argument before reading the image. Directory extraction
was added in [erofs-utils 1.5](https://lkml.iu.edu/2206.1/05030.html), and tar input
in [1.7](https://lkml.iu.edu/2309.2/05170.html). Removing the destination argument
would leave the files needed by the builder unextracted.

Check which tools your terminal selects:

```sh
command -v fsck.erofs mkfs.erofs
fsck.erofs -V
```

Upgrade both tools to a compatible package from your distribution. If its package
is too old, build the tested release in your home directory using the
[upstream build procedure](https://erofs.docs.kernel.org/en/latest/install.html).
For Debian/Ubuntu:

```sh
sudo apt-get install build-essential git autoconf automake libtool pkg-config liblz4-dev uuid-dev
mkdir -p "$HOME/.cache/onn2026-host-tools"
git clone --depth 1 --branch v1.7.1 https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/xiang/erofs-utils.git "$HOME/.cache/onn2026-host-tools/erofs-utils-1.7.1"
cd "$HOME/.cache/onn2026-host-tools/erofs-utils-1.7.1"
./autogen.sh
./configure --prefix="$HOME/.local/onn2026-erofs-1.7.1" --enable-lz4
make -j2
make install
export PATH="$HOME/.local/onn2026-erofs-1.7.1/bin:$PATH"
fsck.erofs -V
```

If you already cloned that release, use the existing source folder. Check that
each build command succeeds before continuing. `make install` uses the home
directory prefix above and needs no `sudo`.

In that same terminal, return to the installer checkout and rerun
`python3 onn2026.py`. Keep its existing `work/` folder and select the same onn;
the guide resumes the build using its saved unlock and patch records. Export
the same `PATH` again if you open a new terminal. If you previously selected
explicit tool paths, those saved paths must point to compatible binaries too.
